Part of #295

## Question

Evaluate `vercel/chat` (`chat`, `@chat-adapter/slack`, `@chat-adapter/teams`) inside SurveyBeat's Cloudflare Workers + Alchemy + Effect 4.1.x toolchain (`nodejs_compat`, `packages/cloudflare`). Compare it against thin custom Effect adapters for Slack and Microsoft Teams.

Check specifically:
- Workerd compatibility and bundle footprint for Slack and Teams adapters.
- Webhook signature verification and stateless request handling in `MainWorker`.
- Whether a Durable Object SQLite `StateAdapter` is needed for our outbound-first + slash-command surface.
- Card rendering fidelity (Slack Block Kit and Teams Adaptive Cards) for Invitation cards with 1-tap Answer links, Reminders, and Shared Results summaries.
- Slack app and Microsoft Teams bot/app registration & OAuth installation requirements per Organization.

## Output

A written research note recommending `vercel/chat` or thin custom adapters, with concrete constraints for the Channel delivery ADR.

## Also check (added in review, 2026-11-20)

- **State storage:** does `vercel/chat` need Redis or another external store for state? A third-party store would break the Cloudflare-only rule (SPEC §6), so the answer decides whether a Durable Object SQLite `StateAdapter` is required.
- **Teams proactive messages:** what sending an Invitation unprompted needs, such as an Azure Bot registration and a stored conversation reference per user, and where that reference lives (D1 or the Organization Durable Object).
- **Microsoft Teams Safe Links:** test whether Safe Links keeps the URL fragment `#t=…&v=…` on a link to `answer.html`. If it does not, Teams Invitations offer "Open check-in" only.
- **Slack interaction events:** confirm that plain message links (no Block Kit buttons) send no `block_actions` or other event to our request URL when clicked.

## Destination

Release 3 "Reach and close the loop" is ready to build for small Teams first: Channel-agnostic delivery across Email, Slack, and Microsoft Teams; Action follow-up Questions and Comment theme deep-dives; Core + Rotating Questions; and a privacy-enforced remote MCP server. Every hard-to-reverse decision is recorded in ADRs (`docs/adr/`), `SPEC.md §8` is updated to reflect the re-sequencing, `GLOSSARY.md` carries any new terms, and R3 is split into implementation-sized issues under a "Release 3: implementation" tracking issue.

## Notes

- Domain: `SPEC.md` is the source, `GLOSSARY.md` the vocabulary, ADRs 0001–0026 bind. Use glossary terms in every ticket (Pulse, Round, Person, Lead, Submission, Answer, Minimum group size, Comment theme, Discussion guide, Action, Review window, Channel, Distribution, Redaction).
- Planning only. No production code. Throwaway spikes are allowed as `prototype` or `task` tickets when a decision depends on one.
- Trust before features (`SPEC.md §3.1`): when a choice trades anonymity for convenience, anonymity wins. Anything sent to a third party is a new data flow and must be stated plainly to members.
- Cloudflare-only runtime (`SPEC.md §6`): everything runs on Cloudflare Workers + Durable Objects + D1. No long-running Node container or third-party cloud relay (ruling out `CopilotKit/channels-sdk` + CopilotKit Intelligence).

## Decisions so far

- **Small Teams first (product owner, 2026-11-20):** Re-sequence `SPEC.md §8` to ship small-Team habit and loop-closing features ahead of enterprise Organizations (SCIM, nested Teams, cross-Team comparisons, Confidential mode).
- **Channel-agnostic delivery — Slack + Microsoft Teams + Email (product owner, 2026-11-20):** Use a serverless, Cloudflare Workers-compatible multi-channel layer (evaluating `vercel/chat` vs thin Effect adapters) behind a domain `ChannelSender` port, starting with Slack and Microsoft Teams plus Email as the built-in fallback. Zero-Leakage Handoff: chat Channels deliver Invitations (with 1-tap first-Question links), Reminders, and Shared Results summaries, while Answers still confirm on `answer.html` through the zero-observability `SubmissionWorker` (preserving ADR 0005).
- **Closing the loop & anti-fatigue (product owner, 2026-11-20):** Pull up Action follow-up Questions, one-click Comment theme deep-dive Questions (privacy-safe alternative to server-linked 1:1 anonymous chat), and Core + Rotating Questions into Release 3.
- **Remote MCP server privacy default (product owner, 2026-11-20):** Raw redacted comments are **off by default** over MCP (default exposes scores, Comment themes, Actions, Notes, and Lead-only Discussion guide), with an opt-in Organization setting for raw redacted comments. Organization admins still see no Results (ADR 0003).

## Not yet specified

- **Legal text for the new data flows.** Release 3 slices must describe the Slack, Microsoft Teams and MCP data flows on the privacy page and in legal text, but the public legal pages and the sub-processor register do not exist yet ([GDPR: Public legal pages (Privacy Notice, Terms, DPA, Sub-processors) and in-app transparency](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/305)). Whether Slack and Microsoft count as SurveyBeat sub-processors or as the customer's own tools, and which ticket owns that text, waits on the Channel delivery design.
- **Data subject rights for new personal data.** Chat identity links (email ↔ chat user), workspace installations and MCP OAuth grants are new personal data. Export and erasure ([GDPR: Right of Access and Portability — personal data export (Art. 15, Art. 20)](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/306), [GDPR: Right to Erasure — true personal data deletion for People (Art. 17)](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/307)) must cover them once their storage is decided.
- **Teams fallback shape.** If research finds that Microsoft Teams Safe Links drops the URL fragment, the "Open check-in"-only Teams Invitation may need its own UX decision.

## Out of scope

- Enterprise Organizations release (deferred to Release 4): Enterprise SSO / SCIM Directory Sync, nested Teams and subtraction-safe roll-ups, standard Questions and cross-Team comparison, Confidential mode, Audit log, CSV/PDF exports.
- Issue tracker sync for Actions (Linear / Jira / GitHub Issues) and public REST API / webhooks.
- In-chat Answer submission that routes Answers through Slack/Teams webhooks or `MainWorker` (revisit only via a dedicated ADR if teams ask for it).

## Review of the child tickets (2026-11-20)

The product owner accepted every recommendation from the review. Each ticket's body holds its part:

- #300 and #302 are now blocked by #299.
- Chat Invitations use plain links only and turn link previews off; the message is edited to remove answer links once the member answers or the Round closes (#298).
- Results summaries post only once the Result is shared, without comments, counts or the Discussion guide (#298).
- MCP serves Leads only, checks that the Person is active and not banned, and turning on raw comments adds a line to the answer page's anonymity statement (#301, #302).
- Round order: core, then rotating, then One-Round Questions, so Question 1 stays a rating (#299, #300).
- Release 4 = Enterprise Organizations, Release 5 = Public API, webhooks, "Ask your results", issue-tracker sync. Slack ships before Teams within Release 3. "Live Redaction Preview" is dropped (#296).

content.content:
## 5. Functional requirements

Requirements are grouped by the loop step they serve. Section 8 sequences them into releases.

### 5.1 Ask: set up and send pulses

- A lead can create a pulse in under two minutes by starting from a template. The product ships with templates for weekly team health, sprint retrospectives, onboarding check-ins (at 30, 60, and 90 days), and a manager feedback round.
- Question types are rating (1 to 5, with labeled ends), eNPS (0 to 10), single choice, multiple choice, short text, and long text. Each rating question can have an optional "Want to say more?" comment field.
- The question library is shared across the organization. Admins can mark questions as standard, so that every team asking the same question produces comparable data across the organization.
- The pulse editor shows an estimated answer time, and warns when a pulse goes over 7 questions or about 90 seconds.
- Optional rotation. A pulse can have a fixed core set of questions plus a rotating set, where each round asks one or two different questions. This covers more topics without making each round longer.
- Cadence uses each member's local time zone. Monday 9:00 means 9:00 for each recipient. A lead can skip a round (for holidays) or pause a pulse.
- Channels are email, Slack, and Microsoft Teams. Each member picks their preferred channel. Email is the fallback for everyone.
- The first question can be answered directly from the message. In email, each rating value is a link that opens the answer page with that value chosen; the answer is saved when the member confirms it there, because email security scanners open every link (ADR 0007). In Slack and Teams, the message has interactive buttons and, where the platform allows it, a modal for the rest.
- Reminders go only to members who have not answered, and there are at most two per round. A member can turn reminders off.
- A shareable link remains available for teams that do not use invitations. A link round cannot compute a response rate and cannot guarantee one answer per person. The UI says so.

### 5.2 Answer: the member experience

- The answer page loads in under one second on a mid-range phone on 4G. It needs no sign-in when opened from an invitation token. It does need sign-in when opened from the shared link, if the organization requires it.
- One question per screen on mobile. All questions on one page on desktop. Keyboard navigation works fully. The page meets WCAG 2.2 AA.
- The answer page states the round's anonymity mode in plain words before the first question, along with what the lead will and will not see. Example: "Your lead sees the team's combined answers once at least 4 people respond. Your name is never stored with your answers."
- A member can change answers until the round closes. In anonymous rounds this needs a design that does not link the person to the submission on the server. The recommended approach is a random edit key that only the member's browser stores. If the member loses the key, they cannot edit, and that is acceptable.
- After submitting, the member sees a thank-you screen and the team's current open actions. This reminds them that answering leads to change.
- A member has a private history page that shows their own past attributed answers. It also shows their anonymous answers if their browser still holds those edit keys. Nobody else can see this page.
- Interface language is English only for now (ADR 0025; German was planned for Release 2 under ADR 0018). All strings must be translatable from day one.

### 5.7 Integrations and API

- **Slack app and Microsoft Teams app.** Members can answer from the messages. Leads get the results summary in a channel they choose. A slash command or message action shows the team's current health.
- **Public API.** A small, versioned HTTP API, authenticated with organization API keys, that returns results and actions. All privacy rules apply.
- **MCP server.** A remote MCP server lets a lead use an AI assistant to ask about their teams' results and manage actions. It enforces the same permissions and privacy thresholds as the web app, because it calls the same domain services.
- **Webhooks.** Webhooks for "round results ready" and "action created or updated".

### 5.8 Product surfaces outside the app

- A marketing landing page, a pricing page that can be a placeholder, and legal pages for privacy, terms, and the data processing agreement. The old app had legal page stubs. The rebuild needs real text before any external customer uses it.
- Transactional emails for invitations, reminders, results-ready notices, and action updates. They must look good in the major email clients and in dark mode.

## 6. Platform and architecture

Everything runs on Cloudflare. No Next.js, no Vercel, and no separate cloud provider for compute or data. Sign-in runs on Better Auth inside the Main Worker, so the Slack and Microsoft Teams platforms are the only required external services.

### 6.1 Fixed technology choices

| Concern | Choice | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Infrastructure as code | alchemy.run | Every Cloudflare resource, binding, secret, and custom domain is declared in TypeScript with Alchemy. No dashboard changes. No Terraform. No hand-edited wrangler config. |
| Runtime | Cloudflare Workers | One Worker serves the API and the static web app (Workers static assets). Add more Workers only when a job needs a different runtime profile, such as a queue consumer. |
| Business logic | Effect | All domain logic, data access, and integrations are Effect programs. Errors, dependencies, retries, and timeouts are typed. Domain services are Effect services with layers that can be swapped in tests. |
| Schemas | Effect Schema | One schema definition per domain type is shared by the API, the client, the database layer, and the AI tool definitions. External data is parsed at the boundary, and internal code trusts the types. |
| HTTP API | Effect's platform HTTP API module | The API is declared once. The server implementation and a typed client for the web app both come from that declaration. |
| Web app | React single-page app built with Vite | Client-side routing with a typed router, such as TanStack Router. Answer pages and email landing pages must render fast without a heavy bundle. Split them into their own small entry point. |
| UI components | Base UI | Unstyled, accessible primitives. Build a small design system of your own on top (tokens, typography, and a dozen composed components). Tailwind CSS for styling is fine. Charts need an accessible library or hand-built SVG, and each chart needs a table view. |
| Authentication | Better Auth on D1, email codes | The Worker serves `/auth/*`: an email-code start and verify, a session cookie, and sign-out. The session is checked on every request against D1 and the Organization's Durable Object. ADR 0022 and ADR 0023. |
| Email | Cloudflare Email Service | Sends invitations, reminders, and notices. Inbound email routing is optional, for reply-to-answer later. If Cloudflare email sending cannot meet deliverability needs, decide on a fallback and record it. |
| AI | Cloudflare Workers AI, through AI Gateway | Comment redaction, theme grouping, discussion guides, and "ask your results". AI Gateway handles caching, rate limits, logging policy, and model swaps. Never send raw comments to a model that keeps them. |

### 6.2 Cloudflare building blocks and their jobs

The recommended layout follows. Departures are fine when they make the system simpler, but write down the reason.

- **Durable Object per organization, with SQLite storage, as the system of record.** Each organization's people, teams, pulses, rounds, submissions, results, and actions live in that organization's own Durable Object. This gives hard tenant isolation, strongly consistent writes, and plain SQL for analytics within one organization. Survey data is small, so a single object's storage limit is far away. An organization with 5,000 people answering weekly for 5 years stays well under it. Check this number against current Cloudflare limits before you commit.
- **Durable Object per open round** (optional, decide during the build). It counts participation, rejects double submissions, and owns the round's state machine. If the organization object handles this load well, skip the extra object.
- **D1 for the global index.** This holds what must be looked up before you know the organization: auth user to Persons, invitation token to organization and round, Slack and Teams workspace to organization, and API keys. Keep it small. No survey content goes here.
- **Cloudflare Workflows for the round lifecycle.** Each round is a durable workflow. It waits until the open time, sends invitations in batches, waits, sends reminders, closes, computes results, and notifies. Workflows give retries and resumption after crashes, and each step must be idempotent.
- **Cron Triggers** run once an hour to create the next round for each active pulse. This job is idempotent. Running it twice creates no duplicate rounds.
- **Queues** buffer outbound messages (email, Slack, Teams) and inbound webhooks, with retries and a dead-letter queue.
- **R2** stores exports and generated PDFs, and backups of each organization's data on a schedule.
- **KV** holds rarely changing configuration and caches, if needed. Do not use it for sessions that must be revoked at once.
- **Workers Analytics Engine** stores product metrics (send counts, open rates, answer latency). It must never contain answers.
- **Turnstile** protects the public link answer page against bots.
- **Secrets Store, or Worker secrets managed through Alchemy**, holds the Slack and Teams credentials.

### 6.3 Code organization

- One repository and one package manager workspace. Suggested packages are the domain (pure Effect services and schemas, with no Cloudflare imports), the Cloudflare adapters (Durable Objects, D1, Queues, Workflows, and email, each implementing a domain interface), the API, the web app, the infrastructure definition, and the email templates.
- The domain package must run in plain Node tests without Cloudflare. Adapter packages are tested against local Cloudflare emulation (Miniflare, through Alchemy's dev mode or the Vitest integration for Workers).
- Organize modules by domain concept (rounds, privacy, results, actions), not by layer or execution step.

### 6.4 Environments and delivery

- Alchemy stages give every pull request its own preview environment, with its own Workers, D1, and Durable Object namespaces. The preview is removed when the pull request closes.
- `staging` and `production` are Alchemy stages too. Production deploys from the main branch after CI passes.
- CI runs type checking, linting, unit tests, Worker integration tests, the privacy test suite, and an accessibility check on the answer page.
- Errors and traces go to Workers Logs and Workers Observability. Add Sentry only if Cloudflare's tooling is not enough, and then strip all answer content before sending.

# Anonymous Submissions store no person and no time, and are unlinkable at rest, not against a restore

**Threat model.** The Lead, Organization admins, and anyone using the product (UI, API, exports) must never be able to link a member to their Submission, and neither can an operator reading stored data, dumps, or R2 backups. We do **not** claim to defend against an operator who restores the Durable Object to a past moment (point-in-time recovery replays every write, including the one transaction that writes a Participation record and its Submission), reads Cloudflare's internal edge logs, or changes the code to start logging. Against that we use controls instead: only named people can trigger a restore, the privacy page states the 30-day restore window, and code changes on the submission path need review. The answer page's "Your name is never stored with your answers" is true of everything stored.

**Design.**
- Everything lives in the Organization's Durable Object. There is no per-Round object. The first Answer writes the Participation record and a Submission holding that one Answer in **one transaction**, which is how a double submission is rejected (a unique Participation record per Round and Person).
- An anonymous Submission stores only its Round, its Answers, and an Edit key hash. It stores **no person, no Invitation, and no time at all**, not even the day SPEC allows. A Participation record stores Round, Person, and the fact of answering, also with no time.
- Submission and Answer tables are `WITHOUT ROWID` with random 128-bit keys. Reads aggregate or sort by the random key. Dumps and backups are written in key order.
- **The anonymous Submission table has no person column, ever.** Attributed Submissions get their own table, so no bug can put a name on an anonymous answer.
- The Invitation token travels in the **URL fragment**, so the answer page GET (and every link scanner) never sends it. The page POSTs it to a **separate Submission Worker** with logs, traces, tail, Logpush, and Analytics Engine writes all off. That Worker logs error codes only. Tokens are stored only as hashes.
- The **browser generates the Edit key** and sends only its SHA-256 hash with the first Answer. Later Answers and changes carry only the Edit key. **No request may carry both an Invitation token and an Edit key**, and the server rejects one that does.

## Considered Options

- **Submissions in a separate Durable Object.** Rejected: without one transaction, a crash either loses the Answer or allows a second Submission, and the timing gap still exists.
- **Shuffled batch writes.** Rejected: buffered Answers are lost if the object is evicted, and it defends only against the restore threat we don't claim to cover.
- **A nullable person column shared with attributed mode.** Rejected: a single bug would put names on anonymous answers.

## Consequences

Response and answer counts come from Participation records. Answer latency is measured only in tests on a preview stage. Deleting a Person deletes their Participation records, and their anonymous Submissions survive. A member who loses the Edit key cannot change their answers, and that is accepted.
# A one-tap rating link only preselects; the answer is saved when the member confirms it

SPEC §5.1 said each rating link in an email "records the answer". Email security scanners (Microsoft Defender runs headless Chrome) fetch every link, so recording on GET would count scanners as voters. Some scanners can also produce trusted events, so saving on any interaction would still be unsafe. A rating link (`/a#t=<token>&v=<1–5>`) therefore opens the answer page with that value preselected and writes nothing. The answer is saved only when the member taps "Save and continue", which sits directly under the anonymity statement, or changes the value. A member who taps in the email and leaves without touching the page loses that answer. We accept that loss as the price of never counting a scanner.

## Consequences

- The token exchange that loads the page has no side effects, so R1 has no open tracking at all.
- The anonymity statement is always read before the first Answer is stored.
- One-tap needs a rating Question first in the Pulse. Otherwise the email offers only "Open check-in".
# Workspace layout and toolchain: pnpm, TypeScript 7, oxc tools, and Alchemy v2's Effect runtime kept inside the adapters

> Partly superseded by ADR 0011 (the app entry uses Foldkit, not React and Base UI), ADR 0012 (`packages/cloudflare` depends on `packages/emails`), and ADR 0013 (domain folder layout). The rest stands.

**Workspace.** pnpm workspaces with a `catalog:` of exact pins, on Node 24 LTS (`.node-version`). Pinned at: `effect` and all `@effect/*` 4.1.2, `alchemy` and `@alchemy.run/*` 2.0.0-beta.85, `typescript` 7.0.2, and exact `oxlint`, `oxlint-tsgolint`, and `oxfmt` versions. The Effect and Alchemy pins move only together, in a PR of their own, because both are marked unstable or beta.

**Packages.**

| Package | Holds | May depend on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/domain` | Schemas and services by concept (`people/`, `pulses/`, `rounds/`, `answering/`, `results/`, `actions/`, `privacy/`), schedule and Result calculations | `effect` only |
| `packages/api` | The HttpApi declaration shared by server and client | `domain` |
| `packages/cloudflare` | Adapters (Organization DO, D1, Queue consumer, `EmailSender`, alarm scheduler) and the two Worker entries: the main Worker and the Submission Worker | `domain`, `api`, Alchemy runtime |
| `apps/web` | One Vite 8 project with two entries: the app (React, TanStack Router, Base UI) and the answer page (no React, no HttpApi client: plain `fetch` plus shared Schemas) | `api`, `domain` (Schemas) |
| `packages/emails` | Email templates | `domain` |
| `infra` | The Alchemy stack and stages (`pr-<n>`, `staging`, `production`) | everything |

**Cloudflare runtime.** Workers, the Durable Object, the Queue consumer, and Cron are defined with Alchemy v2's Effect runtime, but only in `packages/cloudflare`. If the beta fails us, replacing it with a hand-written bridge of about 100 lines touches only that package.

**Tooling.**
- TypeScript 7.0.2 (the native compiler) with `tsc -b` and project references. Settings: `strict`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `moduleResolution: "bundler"`.
- `@effect/tsgo` provides Effect diagnostics.
- oxfmt formats. oxlint lints, with type-aware rules from `oxlint-tsgolint`.
- A local `jsPlugins` package, `tools/oxlint-plugin-surveybeat`, bans `cloudflare:*` and Alchemy imports in `domain` and `api`, and holds the privacy query lint (no `rowid`, no unordered reads of anonymous tables, no joins between anonymous tables and Participation or Invitation).
- The boundary is also enforced by dependencies: `domain` declares only `effect` and uses `types: []`.

**Tests.** Vitest with `@effect/vitest` everywhere:
- domain and API tests in plain Node with in-memory layers and `HttpApiTest`;
- adapter tests through `@alchemy.run/test` `Test.make({ dev: true })` on local workerd;
- smoke tests with `Test.make()` on the PR stage;
- Playwright end-to-end tests on the PR stage.

`vitest-pool-workers` is not used, and there is no hand-edited wrangler config.

**Answer entry (measured in the answer-page prototype, 2026-11-07).** The answer entry is prerendered static HTML with inline CSS and a small plain TypeScript controller, with no React, Preact, or Base UI. Measured with Lighthouse mobile (slow 4G, 4× CPU), the time until the Question text appears was 1.12 s with this approach, 1.35 s with Preact, 1.61 s with React, and 1.90 s with React plus Base UI. The token request starts from an inline script in `<head>`, and Effect Schema (23.5 KB gzip) loads after first paint. Budget: JS ≤ 10 KB gzip on the critical path, CSS ≤ 2 KB inline, HTML ≤ 8 KB, 1 request before first paint and 2 before the Question text. A Lighthouse CI gate checks FCP ≤ 800 ms, LCP ≤ 1.3 s, and TBT ≤ 50 ms.

## Considered Options

- **TypeScript 5.9 or 6.** Rejected: 7.0.2 is npm `latest`, Effect recommends it, and Alchemy is built against it. 6.0 is the end of the JavaScript-based compiler line. Our tools (oxc, Vite/rolldown, Vitest) don't depend on the old compiler API.
- **Biome, or ESLint with Prettier.** Rejected in favour of oxlint and oxfmt. oxlint's `jsPlugins` let the boundary and privacy rules be ordinary lint rules, and `oxlint-tsgolint` gives type-aware rules on TypeScript 7.
- **A hand-written Effect bridge from day one.** Deferred: Alchemy's runtime removes the bridge code. Keeping it in one package makes the switch cheap if we need it.

## Consequences

A spike on a preview stage verifies this before the walking skeleton is built. It checks the Organization DO with `SqliteClient`, transactions, migrations, and an alarm, a Queue consumer with a dead-letter queue, the Submission Worker with every log setting off, the deployed cold start, and `tsc -b` with project references on TypeScript 7.0.2.
# Email link scanners and one-tap answer links

Research for issue #11 (map #1). This is throwaway research and will not be merged.
Context: SPEC.md §5.1 says "In email, each rating value is a link that records the answer and opens the remaining questions." §5.2 says the answer page needs no sign-in when opened from an invitation token. §5.3 restricts what the submission path may store and log.

Researched 2026-11-07. Each claim cites its source. Claims marked *(secondary)* come from a GitHub issue, a forum, or a search-index summary, not from vendor documentation.

## TL;DR

1. **Scanners request every link in the message, often before the member sees it.** Microsoft Defender scans URLs before delivery and detonates URLs that lack a reputation. Mimecast and Proofpoint sandbox suspicious messages before delivery. All of them, Barracuda and Gmail included, also check the link when it is clicked. A rating email with five links can therefore get five "answers" within seconds.
2. **Scanners send GET and HEAD, and some run a full headless Chrome that executes JavaScript.** Microsoft's requests have been observed from AS8075 with a HeadlessChrome user agent and no cookies *(secondary)*. Running JavaScript on page load is therefore not proof that a human is there. Field reports agree that scanners do not submit forms or click buttons, but no vendor guarantees it.
3. **HTTP itself rules this out.** RFC 9110 says a resource whose URI selects an unsafe action "MUST disable or disallow that action when it is accessed using a safe request method." RFC 8058 introduced POST for one-click unsubscribe for exactly this reason.
4. **Vendors that record the answer on the click get scanner answers.** SurveyMonkey records on click only if you opt in, and its docs warn that scanner bots then answer first. Qualtrics documents the same failure and sells a fix based on reCAPTCHA v3. Medallia gates its auto-save behind bot detection plus a real user interaction. Magic-link providers have moved to codes (WorkOS), bot detection (Stytch), or a GET page plus POST (Supabase, Auth.js, several OSS projects).
5. **Recommendation for SurveyBeat:** the rating link GET opens the answer page with the tapped value preselected and writes nothing. The answer is saved by a POST that a real interaction triggers. It never fires on page load alone. Answer HEAD requests with a 200 that has no side effects. Keep scanner heuristics as a secondary signal for metrics only, never as the gate. Do not store a "tentative" answer on the server. Details follow.

## 1. How the scanners behave

### Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Safe Links

Source: [Safe Links overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/safe-links-about) (updated 2026-10).

- **Pre-delivery scan of every message:** "As long as Safe Links protection is turned on, URLs are scanned prior to message delivery, regardless of whether the URLs are rewritten or not."
- **Detonation:** "URLs that don't have a valid reputation are detonated asynchronously in the background." A new survey domain with per-recipient token URLs is exactly the kind of URL that lacks a reputation.
- **Delivery can wait for the scan:** the recommended setting is "Wait for URL scanning to complete before delivering the message". "Messages are delivered only after the URLs are confirmed to be safe."
- **Click-time check:** links are rewritten to `*.safelinks.protection.outlook.com`. "If a users clicks a rewritten link, it's scanned for malicious content before directing the user to the page." In API-only mode, Outlook clients call Safe Links when the user clicks. The member's own click can therefore cause a second fetch by the scanner just before the browser request.
- **Built-in protection preset:** this preset applies Safe Links to every recipient in any tenant with at least one Defender for Office 365 license, even if no policy was configured. Assume it is on for most Microsoft 365 business customers.
- **Allowlisting:** each policy has a "Do not rewrite the following URLs" list, but its entries "might still be blocked at time of click". The Tenant Allow/Block List covers both delivery and click time. Both are tenant-admin actions, so we cannot rely on them.
- **Methods and fingerprint *(secondary)*:** Auth.js says Safe Links "send a HEAD request to each link in the Email" ([Auth.js tutorial](https://next-auth.js.org/tutorials/avoid-corporate-link-checking-email-provider)). An emdash bug report logged GETs from Microsoft's AS8075 with a headless Chrome user agent and no cookies. The report later saw four GET and HEAD requests within about 90 seconds ([emdash#3298](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/issues/3298)). Microsoft does not publish the scanner's IP ranges or user agents.
- **Real-world precedent *(secondary)*:** in a Microsoft Tech Community thread, Safe Links scans were unsubscribing users from lists. Another participant reported that the scanning "triggered satisfaction ratings in their service desk software" ([thread](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/discussions/microsoft-security/atp-safe-links-are-automatically-unsubscribing-users-from-email-lists/205278/replies/207403)). That second report is the SurveyBeat failure mode.

content.content:
# Chat SDK

> npm package: [`chat`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/chat)

[![Agent Stack](https://img.shields.io/badge/Agent%20Stack-000?style=flat-square&logo=vercel&logoColor=FFF&labelColor=000&color=000)](https://vercel.com/kb/agent-stack)
[![MIT License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-000?style=flat-square&logo=opensourceinitiative&logoColor=white&labelColor=000&color=000)](../../LICENSE)

Universal TypeScript SDK for building multi-platform chat bots and AI agents on Slack, Teams, Google Chat, Discord, WhatsApp, and more. Provides the `Chat` class, event handlers, JSX cards, emoji helpers, and type-safe message formatting.

Documentation: [chat-sdk.dev/docs](https://chat-sdk.dev/docs) · Guides: [vercel.com/kb/chat-sdk](https://vercel.com/kb/chat-sdk)

## Installation

```bash
npm install chat
```

## CLI

Scaffold a minimal Next.js bot app with `create-chat-sdk`:

```bash
npx create-chat-sdk@latest my-bot
```

The CLI generates your `Chat` configuration, webhook route, `.env.example` file, dependencies, and optional Web adapter route from the adapter catalog. See the [CLI docs](https://chat-sdk.dev/docs/create-chat-sdk) for options and non-interactive usage.

## Usage

```typescript
import { Chat } from "chat";
import { createSlackAdapter } from "@chat-adapter/slack";
import { createRedisState } from "@chat-adapter/state-redis";

const bot = new Chat({
  userName: "mybot",
  adapters: {
    slack: createSlackAdapter({
      botToken: process.env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN!,
      signingSecret: process.env.SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET!,
    }),
  },
  state: createRedisState({ url: process.env.REDIS_URL! }),
  dedupeTtlMs: 600_000, // 10 minutes (default: 5 min)
});

bot.onNewMention(async (thread) => {
  await thread.subscribe();
  await thread.post("Hello! I'm listening to this thread.");
});

bot.onSubscribedMessage(async (thread, message) => {
  await thread.post(`You said: ${message.text}`);
});
```

> **Tip:** PostgreSQL and ioredis adapters are also available for production. See [State Adapters](https://chat-sdk.dev/docs/state-adapters) for all options.

## Configuration

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `userName` | `string` | **required** | Default bot username across all adapters |
| `adapters` | `Record<string, Adapter>` | **required** | Map of adapter name to adapter instance |
| `state` | `StateAdapter` | **required** | State adapter for subscriptions, locking, and dedup |
| `logger` | `Logger \| LogLevel` | `"info"` | Logger instance or log level (`"silent"` to disable) |
| `streamingUpdateIntervalMs` | `number` | `500` | Update interval for fallback streaming (post + edit) in ms |
| `dedupeTtlMs` | `number` | `300000` | TTL for message deduplication entries in ms. Increase if webhook cold starts cause platform retries (e.g., Slack's `http_timeout` retry) that arrive after the default window |

## AI Coding Agents

If you use an AI coding agent such as OpenAI Codex, Claude Code, or Cursor, install the Chat SDK skill so it knows the SDK APIs, adapter patterns, and project conventions before writing code.

```bash
npx skills add vercel/chat
```

The skill references bundled documentation in `node_modules/chat/docs`, plus adapter guides and starter templates in the published package.

You can also install the [Vercel Plugin](https://vercel.com/docs/agent-resources/vercel-plugin) for a broader agent toolkit — it includes the Chat SDK skill alongside specialist agents, agent slash commands, and more:

```bash
npx plugins add vercel/vercel-plugin
```

The plugin is optional; the skill alone is enough to build with Chat SDK.

For agent-readable documentation, see [chat-sdk.dev/llms.txt](https://chat-sdk.dev/llms.txt) (page index) or [chat-sdk.dev/llms-full.txt](https://chat-sdk.dev/llms-full.txt) (full text).

## Documentation

Full documentation is available at [chat-sdk.dev/docs](https://chat-sdk.dev/docs).

- [Usage](https://chat-sdk.dev/docs/usage) — event handlers, threads, messages, channels
- [Chat API](https://chat-sdk.dev/docs/api/chat) — full `Chat` class reference
- [Cards](https://chat-sdk.dev/docs/cards) — JSX-based interactive cards
- [Streaming](https://chat-sdk.dev/docs/streaming) — AI SDK integration
- [Emoji](https://chat-sdk.dev/docs/emoji) — cross-platform emoji helpers

content.content:
---
title: State Adapters
description: State adapters store thread subscriptions, distributed locks, and cached data for your bot.
type: overview
prerequisites:
  - /docs/getting-started
related:
  - /docs/concurrency
  - /docs/history
  - /docs/testing
---

State adapters store thread subscriptions, distributed locks, and cached data. Every `Chat` instance needs one. Browse the available state adapters on the [Adapters](/adapters) page.

## What state adapters manage

### Thread subscriptions

When your bot calls `thread.subscribe()`, the state adapter persists that subscription. On later webhooks, the SDK checks it to route messages to `onSubscribedMessage`. With a production adapter such as Redis or PostgreSQL, subscriptions survive restarts and are shared across instances.

### Distributed locking

When a message arrives, the SDK acquires a lock on its thread, or on its channel for adapters that lock per channel, such as WhatsApp and Telegram. The lock stops two handlers from processing messages in the same thread at once, even when your bot runs on several serverless instances.

The `concurrency` option decides what happens when the lock is already held. By default, the new message is dropped with a `LockError`. You can also queue it, debounce a burst of messages, or skip locking entirely. See [Concurrency](/docs/concurrency) for the strategies and for [lock scope](/docs/concurrency#lock-scope).

The deprecated `onLockConflict` option still works under the default `drop` strategy. Set it to `'force'` to release the held lock and let the new message through, for example so a new message can interrupt a long-running AI response:

```typescript
const chat = new Chat({
  userName: 'my-bot',
  adapters: { slack },
  state: createRedisState(),
  onLockConflict: 'force',
});
```

You can also pass a callback that decides per message:

```typescript
onLockConflict: (threadId, message) => {
  return message.text.includes('stop') ? 'force' : 'drop';
}
```

Force-releasing a lock doesn't cancel the previous handler. It keeps running without the lock, so two handlers can briefly run on the same thread at the same time.

### Caching and storage

State adapters also provide key-value storage with a TTL. The SDK uses it for thread and channel state (`thread.setState()`), for message deduplication, which ignores webhooks a platform delivers more than once, and for internal caches. Lists back the [History API](/docs/history), and queues back the `queue`, `debounce`, and `burst` concurrency strategies.

To build your own state adapter, implement the `StateAdapter` interface exported from `chat`. The `@chat-adapter/state-memory` package is a small implementation you can use as a reference.

## Production state on Vercel

The [Memory](/adapters/official/memory) adapter keeps state in process memory, so it suits local development and tests. In production, use [Redis](/adapters/official/redis), [ioredis](/adapters/official/ioredis), or [PostgreSQL](/adapters/official/postgres) so subscriptions, locks, and cached data are shared across instances and survive restarts.

If you deploy to Vercel, you can provision either database from the [Vercel Marketplace](https://vercel.com/marketplace/category/storage) with the Vercel CLI:

| Provider | Command | State adapter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Upstash Redis | `vercel integration add upstash/upstash-kv` | [Redis](/adapters/official/redis#vercel-marketplace) or [ioredis](/adapters/official/ioredis) |
| Redis Cloud | `vercel integration add redis` | [Redis](/adapters/official/redis#vercel-marketplace) or [ioredis](/adapters/official/ioredis) |
| Neon | `vercel integration add neon` | [PostgreSQL](/adapters/official/postgres#vercel-marketplace) |
| Supabase | `vercel integration add supabase` | [PostgreSQL](/adapters/official/postgres#vercel-marketplace) |
| Prisma Postgres | `vercel integration add prisma` | [PostgreSQL](/adapters/official/postgres#vercel-marketplace) |
| Nile | `vercel integration add nile` | [PostgreSQL](/adapters/official/postgres#vercel-marketplace) |

Run the command from a linked project directory:

```bash
vercel link
vercel integration add upstash/upstash-kv
```

`vercel integration add` creates the database, connects it to the linked project, adds its credentials as environment variables, and pulls them into your local env file. Each adapter page lists the environment variables the adapter reads and how to pass a different one.

---
title: Overlapping Messages
description: Control how overlapping messages on the same thread are handled, with the burst, queue, debounce, drop, and concurrent strategies.
type: guide
prerequisites:
  - /docs/handling-events
related:
  - /docs/state-adapters
  - /docs/streaming
  - /docs/error-handling
---

When a message arrives on a thread while a handler is still processing an earlier one, the SDK drops the new message by default. The `concurrency` option on `ChatConfig` lets you choose a different strategy.

## Strategies

### Drop (default)

This is the original behavior. If a handler is already running on a thread, the new message is discarded and a `LockError` is thrown. Nothing is queued or retried.

```typescript title="lib/bot.ts"
const bot = new Chat({
  concurrency: "drop",
  // ...
});
```

### Queue

Messages that arrive while a handler is running are enqueued. When the current handler finishes, only the latest queued message is dispatched. The intermediate messages are passed in `context.skipped`, so your handler can see everything that arrived while it was busy.

```typescript title="lib/bot.ts" lineNumbers
const bot = new Chat({
  concurrency: "queue",
  // ...
});

bot.onNewMention(async (thread, message, context) => {
  if (context && context.skipped.length > 0) {
    await thread.post(
      `You sent ${context.totalSinceLastHandler} messages while I was thinking. Responding to your latest.`
    );
  }

  const response = await generateAIResponse(message.text);
  await thread.post(response);
});
```

Flow:

```
A arrives  → acquire lock → process A
B arrives  → lock busy → enqueue B
C arrives  → lock busy → enqueue C
D arrives  → lock busy → enqueue D
A done     → drain: [B, C, D] → handler(D, { skipped: [B, C] })
D done     → queue empty → release lock
```

### Burst

Waits for `debounceMs` before the first handler on an idle thread, then drains the collected burst like `queue`. The latest message is dispatched, and earlier messages in the burst are available as `context.skipped`.

Use this for assistant-style bots where users often send one logical turn as several short messages inside a small window and you want one response with full context. Compared to `debounce`, `burst` keeps the earlier messages in `context.skipped` instead of dropping them, and it flushes queued messages that arrive while the handler is running.

Choose `debounce` when the latest message replaces earlier ones, like rapid corrections. Choose `burst` when earlier messages still matter, like "hey", "quick question", and then the actual question. The tradeoff is that even a lone message waits for `debounceMs` before the handler runs.

```typescript title="lib/bot.ts" lineNumbers
const bot = new Chat({
  concurrency: { strategy: "burst", debounceMs: 1000 },
  // ...
});

bot.onNewMention(async (thread, message, context) => {
  const turn = [...(context?.skipped ?? []), message]
    .map((m) => m.text)
    .join("\n\n");

  const response = await generateAIResponse(turn);

---
title: Adapter Catalog
description: Use @chat-adapter/catalog to list Chat SDK adapters, check their capabilities, and read setup requirements without importing adapter packages.
type: reference
prerequisites:
  - /docs/adapters
related:
  - /docs/platform-adapters
  - /docs/state-adapters
  - /docs/create-chat-sdk
  - /docs/contributing/publishing
  - /docs/contributing/vendor-official
---

`@chat-adapter/catalog` is a static catalog of every adapter listed on chat-sdk.dev: official, vendor-official, and community. It imports no adapter packages, so you can use it from websites, setup screens, build scripts, or onboarding flows without pulling in Slack, Teams, Redis, or other platform SDKs. The [Adapters](/adapters) page and [`create-chat-sdk`](/docs/create-chat-sdk) both read from it.

<Callout type="info">
  The `chat/adapters` subpath is deprecated. It re-exports the original official and vendor-official API from `@chat-adapter/catalog`, so existing imports keep working. Import from `@chat-adapter/catalog` in new code.
</Callout>

## Install

<PackageInstall package="@chat-adapter/catalog" />

## List adapters

List adapters and check what each one supports:

```typescript title="scripts/list-adapters.ts" lineNumbers
import { getFeatureSupport, listAdapters } from "@chat-adapter/catalog";

for (const adapter of listAdapters({ type: "platform" })) {
  const streaming = getFeatureSupport(adapter, "streaming");
  console.log(adapter.name, adapter.group, adapter.packageName, streaming);
}
```

`listAdapters()` returns official and vendor-official adapters in the order the Adapters page lists them, followed by community adapters. Pass `group` or `type` to filter the list.

## Read setup requirements

Official and vendor-official entries also describe setup. Use the env helpers when you need to show setup instructions or inject secrets for one adapter:

```typescript lineNumbers
import { getAdapter, getSecretEnvVars } from "@chat-adapter/catalog";

const slack = getAdapter("slack");
const secrets = getSecretEnvVars("slack").map((envVar) => envVar.key);

console.log(slack.name, slack.factoryExport, secrets);
```

Community entries carry listing metadata and capabilities only, so `listEnvVars()` and `getSecretEnvVars()` return an empty array for them.

## Capabilities

Each entry's `features` field records which Chat SDK capabilities the adapter supports. These are the same values the feature tables on each adapter page show. A value is either a status (`"yes"`, `"no"`, or `"partial"`) or an object with a `status` and a short `label`, such as `{ status: "yes", label: "Native" }`. Omitted keys mean `"no"`.

`getFeatureSupport(adapterOrSlug, key)` always returns the object form. `PLATFORM_FEATURE_CATEGORIES` and `STATE_FEATURE_CATEGORIES` list every capability key with a display label, grouped the way the docs tables group them. `getFeatureCategories(type)` returns the categories for `"platform"` or `"state"`.

[![Microsoft Teams adapter for Chat SDK](https://chat-sdk.dev/en/adapters/official/teams/og)](https://chat-sdk.dev/adapters/official/teams)

# @chat-adapter/teams

> npm package: [`@chat-adapter/teams`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chat-adapter/teams)

[![Agent Stack](https://img.shields.io/badge/Agent%20Stack-000?style=flat-square&logo=vercel&logoColor=FFF&labelColor=000&color=000)](https://vercel.com/kb/agent-stack)
[![MIT License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-000?style=flat-square&logo=opensourceinitiative&logoColor=white&labelColor=000&color=000)](../../LICENSE)

Microsoft Teams adapter for [Chat SDK](https://chat-sdk.dev).

Documentation: [chat-sdk.dev/adapters/official/teams](https://chat-sdk.dev/adapters/official/teams) · Guides: [vercel.com/kb/chat-sdk](https://vercel.com/kb/chat-sdk)

## Installation

```bash
pnpm add @chat-adapter/teams
```

## Scaffold with the CLI

To scaffold a new Microsoft Teams bot with this adapter preselected:

```bash
npx create-chat-sdk@latest my-bot --adapter teams memory
```

Visit the [adapters directory](https://chat-sdk.dev/adapters) to see other available official and vendor-official adapters.

## Quick start

For managed credentials and webhook verification, see [**Vercel Connect**](#option-a--vercel-connect).

The adapter auto-detects `TEAMS_APP_ID`, `TEAMS_APP_PASSWORD`, and `TEAMS_APP_TENANT_ID` from environment variables:

```typescript
import { Chat } from "chat";
import { createTeamsAdapter } from "@chat-adapter/teams";

const bot = new Chat({
  userName: "mybot",
  adapters: {
    teams: createTeamsAdapter({
      appType: "SingleTenant",
    }),
  },
});

bot.onNewMention(async (thread, message) => {
  await thread.post("Hello from Teams!");
});
```

## Configuration

All options are auto-detected from environment variables when not provided. Internally, the adapter maps these options to the Teams SDK (`@microsoft/teams.apps`).

| Option | Required | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| `appId` | No* | Azure Bot App ID or sync/async resolver. Auto-detected from `TEAMS_APP_ID` |
| `appPassword` | No** | Azure Bot App Password. Auto-detected from `TEAMS_APP_PASSWORD` |
| `federated` | No** | Federated (workload identity) authentication config |
| `token` | No** | Custom `(scope, tenantId?)` token factory for Bot Framework and Microsoft Graph |
| `webhookVerifier` | No | Custom raw-body verifier that replaces Microsoft JWT verification |
| `appType` | No | `"MultiTenant"` or `"SingleTenant"` (default: `"MultiTenant"`) |
| `appTenantId` | For SingleTenant | Azure AD Tenant ID. Auto-detected from `TEAMS_APP_TENANT_ID` |
| `userName` | No | Bot display name (default: `"bot"`) |
| `apiUrl` | No | Override the Teams API base URL (e.g. for GCC-High or sovereign-cloud deployments). Auto-detected from `TEAMS_API_URL` |
| `logger` | No | Logger instance (defaults to `ConsoleLogger("info")`) |

\*`appId` is required — either via config or `TEAMS_APP_ID` env var.

\*\*One authentication method is required: `appPassword`, `federated`, or `token`. `token` takes precedence over `federated`, which takes precedence over `appPassword`.

## Authentication

Use Vercel Connect to manage the bot identity and tokens, or configure Microsoft app credentials directly.

### Option A — Vercel Connect

Use [Vercel Connect](https://chat-sdk.dev/docs/vercel-connect) to resolve the bot's app ID and request short-lived tokens for Bot Framework and Microsoft Graph:

```typescript
import { createTeamsAdapter } from "@chat-adapter/teams";
import { connectTeamsAdapter } from "@vercel/connect/chat";

const teams = createTeamsAdapter({
  ...connectTeamsAdapter("microsoft-teams/acme-teams"),
});
```

The helper resolves `appId` during initialization and supplies a scope-aware `token` callback. It also verifies Connect-forwarded webhooks with Vercel OIDC instead of Microsoft's native JWT. Enable trigger forwarding to `/api/webhooks/teams` and omit `TEAMS_APP_ID` and `TEAMS_APP_PASSWORD` when using the helper.

The callback requests separate tokens for `https://api.botframework.com/.default` and `https://graph.microsoft.com/.default`. Graph reads still require the appropriate installation and consent permissions; Connect uses the bot's home tenant for managed tokens.

An `appId` resolver runs once during successful initialization. Call `await bot.initialize()` before using adapter methods directly; Chat initializes automatically before handling webhooks. `botUserId` becomes available after initialization when using a resolver.

A custom `webhookVerifier` receives the incoming request and its raw body. Return a truthy value to accept, or return a falsy value or throw to reject with HTTP 401. Without a verifier, the adapter retains Microsoft's native JWT verification.

### Option B — Microsoft app credentials

The [Teams CLI](https://microsoft.github.io/teams-sdk/cli) handles AAD app registration, client secret generation, bot registration, and Teams channel setup in one command.

```bash
npm install -g @microsoft/teams.cli
```

#### 1. Create the app

```bash
teams login
teams status          # verify auth + sideloading permissions
teams app create --name "My Bot" --endpoint "https://your-domain.com/api/webhooks/teams" --env .env
```

> [!TIP]
> For local development, use a tunnel (e.g. [devtunnel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/developer/dev-tunnels/), ngrok) to expose your local server.

Credentials (`CLIENT_ID`, `CLIENT_SECRET`, `TENANT_ID`) are written to `.env`. Rename them to match the adapter:

```bash
TEAMS_APP_ID=<CLIENT_ID>
TEAMS_APP_PASSWORD=<CLIENT_SECRET>
TEAMS_APP_TENANT_ID=<TENANT_ID>
```

#### 2. Install in Teams

Get a direct install link:

```bash
teams app get <appId> --install-link
```

Or download the app package for sideloading:

```bash
teams app package download <appId> -o my-bot.zip
```

Then in Teams: **Apps** > **Manage your apps** > **Upload an app** > **Upload a custom app**.

#### 3. Verify

```bash
teams app doctor <appId>
```

Checks bot registration, AAD app health, manifest consistency, and endpoint reachability.

#### Credential methods

The adapter supports client-secret, federated, and custom-token authentication. When no explicit auth is provided, `TEAMS_APP_PASSWORD` is auto-detected from environment variables.

##### Client secret (default)

The simplest option — provide `appPassword` directly or set `TEAMS_APP_PASSWORD`:

```typescript
createTeamsAdapter({
  appPassword: "REDACTED",
});
```

##### Federated (workload identity)

For environments with managed identities (e.g. Azure Kubernetes Service, GitHub Actions). Maps to `managedIdentityClientId` in the Teams SDK:

```typescript
createTeamsAdapter({
  federated: {
    clientId: "your_managed_identity_client_id_here",
  },
});
```

##### Custom token factory

Provide `token: (scope, tenantId?) => string | Promise<string>` to acquire tokens externally. The requested scope identifies Bot Framework or Microsoft Graph. This takes precedence over configured credentials and client-secret environment variables, including `CLIENT_SECRET`.

## Environment variables

```bash
TEAMS_APP_ID=...
TEAMS_APP_PASSWORD=...
TEAMS_APP_TENANT_ID=...  # Required for SingleTenant apps
TEAMS_API_URL=...        # Optional, for GCC-High or sovereign-cloud deployments
```

## Mentions

Incoming Teams mentions are supported. Outgoing `@name` text, including multi-word names, stays plain text and does not notify the user. The adapter does not resolve display names into user identities or generate mention entities. Teams requires [matching mention text and entities](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/platform/bots/how-to/conversations/channel-and-group-conversations#add-mentions-to-your-messages) for a real mention; `<at>` markup alone is not sufficient.

## Features

### Messaging

| Feature | Supported |
|---------|-----------|
| Post message | Yes |
| Edit message | Yes |
| Delete message | Yes |
| File uploads | Yes |
| Streaming | Native (DMs) / Buffered fallback (group chats) |

### Rich content

| Feature | Supported |
|---------|-----------|
| Card format | Adaptive Cards |
| Buttons | Yes |
| Link buttons | Yes |
| Select menus | No |
| Tables | Adaptive Card Table |
| Fields | Yes |
| Images in cards | Yes |
| Modals | Yes |

### Conversations

| Feature | Supported |
|---------|-----------|
| Slash commands | No |
| Mentions | Yes |
| Add reactions | Yes |
| Remove reactions | Yes |
| Receive reactions | Yes |
| Typing indicator | Yes |
| DMs | Yes |
| Ephemeral messages | Yes (native targeted messages, public preview) |
| User lookup (`getUser`) | Yes (requires `User.Read.All`) |

### Message history

| Feature | Supported |
|---------|-----------|
| Fetch messages | Yes (requires Graph permissions) |
| Fetch single message | No |
| Fetch thread info | Yes |
| Fetch channel messages | Yes (requires Graph permissions) |
| List threads | Yes (requires Graph permissions) |
| Fetch channel info | Yes (requires Graph permissions) |
| Post channel message | Yes |

## Conversation routing

Incoming thread IDs preserve the Teams conversation type when the legacy ID-prefix heuristic would route it incorrectly. When Teams omits `conversationType`, the adapter falls back to `conversation.isGroup` and the activity's team context. This keeps correctly classified IDs stable while selecting the buffered fallback for group chats whose IDs begin with `a:`. Thread IDs created by older adapter versions remain supported.

## Message edits

`onMessageUpdated` fires when Teams sends the bot an edited message. Teams sends only the new version, so `previousMessage` is `undefined`, and `isMention` comes from the edited message's mentions. `metadata.dateSent` and `metadata.editedAt` are both the edit time, because Teams doesn't send the original send time. Undeleted messages are ignored.

The adapter assumes that a channel edit's `conversation.id` carries `;messageid=<root>`, the same as a new channel message, so the thread ID points at the reply chain. This hasn't been checked against a captured channel edit yet.

In a DM, a stream that an `onMessageUpdated` handler posts goes out as its own message, the same as in group chats and channels. It doesn't use native DM streaming, because that stream belongs to the reply to the original message, which may still be in progress.

## Bot joins

`onMemberJoinedChannel` fires when a `conversationUpdate` activity adds this bot to a channel or group chat. `adapter.botUserId` is the Teams bot ID (`28:<appId>`), so the same bot-join guard works across adapters:

766-| Telegram | Bots can only look up users who have previously messaged them. |
767-| Microsoft Teams | Only works for users who previously interacted with the bot, because profiles are cached from webhook activity. `avatarUrl` is not returned because the Graph API requires a separate photo call. |
768:| Google Chat | Same caching constraint as Teams: only users seen in prior webhooks. |
769-| GitHub | `email` is only returned if the user made it public or you authenticated with the `user:email` scope. |
770-| Linear | Returns the full profile, including email and avatar, for any active workspace member. |
771-| X | Returns the name, username, and avatar. `email` is not returned. Call through the adapter, because X's numeric IDs aren't inferred. |
772-| Twitch | Returns the display name, login, and avatar from Get Users. `email` is not returned. Call through the adapter, because Twitch's numeric IDs aren't inferred. |
773-| Twilio | Doesn't call Twilio. Returns a profile built from the phone number, with the number as `userId`, `userName`, and `fullName`. |

The Teams JWT validator pulled the Microsoft OpenID signing keys from the internet, though none matched the key ID, so the JWT libraries do run under workerd. The Slack slash command handler also calls users.info to fetch a user's profile, which means it pulls personal data. Separately, the adapter logs to the console at info level by default, even though the Teams SDK still logged errors despite logger set to silent.

I'm noting that the log privacy question matters on MainWorker, since observability is on, though these are only warnings. Next I'll look at the top of the workerd output for earlier errors.

content.thinking:
I found that `logger: "silent"` isn't being respected by chat-sdk:slack, which still prints "[chat-sdk:slack] ..." because the adapter creates its own ConsoleLogger defaulting to "info". That explains the leftover output. Next I'm considering how to measure startup CPU against the Workers 1s limit, since timing module evaluation inside workerd is hard and running the bundle under Node would only be a rough estimate.

I'm checking whether the Slack outbound path works under workerd: the earlier users.info call succeeded, so Web API calls should be fine. For Teams, I'd need to see whether acquiring a Bot Framework token with msal-node works there, and I'm thinking about a fake-credential test against the login endpoint to confirm the code path runs. I'm also going to look at how the Teams adapter handles proactive messages, since I don't yet know the thread ID format.

toolu_01EvGBxK5FRVzAWPLmFxNL2A.prompt: Quote verbatim: the signing algorithm (basestring format, HMAC SHA256, header names), the recommended timestamp tolerance (5 minutes) and replay protection advice, and whether raw body must be used.

content.content:
The `url` field description says:

"If you're using url, you'll still receive an interaction payload and will need to send an acknowledgement response."

So clicking a URL button still sends an interaction payload to the app, and the app must acknowledge it. The page doesn't name the `block_actions` payload in this section.

**Signing algorithm**

- **Basestring:** "Concatenate the version number, the timestamp, and the request body together, using a colon (`:`) as a delimiter." The result is `v0:<timestamp>:<body>`.
- **Hash:** "Hash the resulting string, using the signing secret as a key, and taking the hex digest of the hash." The page's wording describes HMAC with SHA-256.
- **Final signature:** It is the hex digest with a `v0=` prefix, which you compare against the request header.
- **Headers:** The signature arrives in `X-Slack-Signature`, and the timestamp is read from `X-Slack-Request-Timestamp`. The page notes that header names are case-insensitive, so you shouldn't assume a letter case.

**Timestamp tolerance and replay protection**

- The example checks that the timestamp is within five minutes of local time, and the code comments say the request "could be a replay attack." The page presents five minutes as the example's threshold rather than a mandated value.
- On replay protection, the page says the signature "depends on the timestamp to protect against replay attacks."

**Raw body**

- Yes, the raw body is required. The page instructs you to "Use the raw request body, without headers, before it has been deserialized from JSON or other forms." In Flask, for example, call `request.get_data()` before accessing other request methods.

**Comparison**

- The page advises using an HMAC compare function rather than a direct equality check.

content.content:
**Interaction types that send payloads to the Request URL** (per the page):

- **`block_actions`**: a user clicks a Block Kit interactive component.
- **`shortcut` and `message_actions`**: a user runs a global or message shortcut.
- **`view_submission`**: a user submits a modal.
- **`view_closed`**: a user cancels a modal.

The page also says each Slash Command has its own Request URL, but it doesn't list a payload type for slash command invocations. Select menus use a separate Options Load URL to fetch menu options, which the page treats as a different mechanism.

**Plain hyperlinks:** The page doesn't mention plain hyperlinks in mrkdwn message text, so it says nothing about whether clicking them sends a payload.

**Acknowledgment requirement:** The page states: "This must be sent within 3 seconds of receiving the payload."

**1. Turning off unfurling and the default for bot-posted messages**

- **Default:** "By default, we unfurl all links in messages posted by users and Slack apps." The doc says this applies to messages posted via incoming webhooks and `chat.postMessage`.
- **Opting out:** To stop unfurling, the doc says to "set both `unfurl_links` and `unfurl_media` to `false`" when posting. It adds that `unfurl_links` covers text-based content and `unfurl_media` covers media, and that the two flags are mutually exclusive.

**2. When an app receives a `link_shared` event**

- The app must register App Unfurl domains (up to five). It "will only receive `link_shared` events for URLs that match your registered domains."
- The `links:read` scope "lets your app read specific links that are posted in Slack."
- The event is not dispatched for messages posted by an app or integration, and an app does not receive events for its own messages.

**3. Does Slack fetch the URL itself?**

For classic unfurling, yes. The doc says "Slack crawls the URL" and that "Our servers must fetch every URL in a message to determine what kind of content it references." For app unfurling, the doc does not say Slack fetches the URL. It sends your app a `link_shared` event, and your app supplies the preview through `chat.unfurl`. The doc does not name a Slackbot crawler.

content.content:
**Bot token scope:** `users:read.email`. The page lists this scope under "Bot token," and it's the same scope required for user tokens.

**Rate limit:** Tier 3, which the page describes as "50+ per minute."

Also note that the page says "Custom bot users cannot use this method."

**Flow summary**

1. **Authorize:** Redirect users to `https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize` (or `https://slack-gov.com/oauth/v2/authorize` for GovSlack) with your client ID and requested scopes. Bot scopes go in `scope`, and user scopes go in `user_scope`.
2. **State check:** "Check the `state` parameter if you sent one along with your initial user redirect." If it doesn't match, treat the authorization as suspect.
3. **Redirect:** Slack sends the user to your Redirect URL with a temporary `code`, which the page says "expires after ten minutes."
4. **Exchange:** Call `oauth.v2.access` with the code, client ID, and client secret to get tokens.

**Response contents**

- A bot access token (`access_token`, with `token_type` set to `bot`), plus any user token under `authed_user`.
- Workspace details in `team.id`. For org-level installs, use `enterprise.id` and `is_enterprise_install`. The page notes: "The `team` property will be `null` for org-level installations where `"is_enterprise_install": true`."

**Token expiration**

"OAuth tokens do not expire." They stop working only when revoked. Token rotation is optional and applies to apps using granular permissions: "you can exchange your access token for a refresh token and an expiring access token with token rotation."

**Installing in other workspaces**

The page doesn't mention "Manage Distribution" or the steps for publicly distributing an app. It does say that an app that isn't publicly distributed can only be installed on the workspace that owns it, unless it's created in an Enterprise org that supports org-wide installation. It also lists `invalid_team_for_non_distributed_app` for installing an undistributed app on a team where it wasn't created. For published apps, it lists `unapproved_scope`, which occurs when requested scopes "aren't approved" because they're still in review or weren't submitted.

**Marketplace listing**

The page doesn't say whether a Marketplace listing is required.
